content.title: Missouri basketball loses first-round NCAA Tournament game to Miami
content.text: Updated March 20, 2026, 11:33 p.m. CTST. LOUIS — It’s the hope, always, that makes it hurt the most.The site of the letdown, this time, was two hours from home. A raucous, Mizzou-leaning crowd filled the Enterprise Center and lived and died with every moment because belief is hard to kick. Dennis Gates turned to his bench with 13:51 to go, down one point after turning a double-digit deficit into a contest, and said, “We’re right there.” He repeated it. He believed it. The crowd got behind those Tigers as it looked oh-so-possible.And ain’t that just always the case?No. 10-seed Missouri basketball lost 80-66 to 7-seed Miami in the first round of the NCAA Tournament on Friday night at Enterprise Center. The Tigers’ season is done, like it has been every year but one since 2010, before the second round of March Madness.Jayden Stone and Anthony Robinson II refused to say die with remarkable plays in the had-to-have-them moments. They finished with 21 and 11 points, respectively.Star forward Mark Mitchell, who had battled double team after double team, pointed to his wrist as a 3-pointer gave Mizzou the lead at the Under-8 media timeout. He finished with 19 points in his final college game.But it’s Miami that had the run to the finish.It’s Miami that will face 2-seed Purdue in the second round of March Madness on Sunday in St. Louis. The Boilermakers beat 15-seed Queens earlier Friday.Miami's Shelton Henderson, who had 14 points, hit the dagger, dropping a wide-open 3-point look to restore a nine-point lead with 4:28 to play. Malik Reneau, who had a game-high 24 points, scored five straight before that to help the Hurricanes to an 11-0 run that ended the Tigers’ dream.Mizzou was in a hole for most of the night.Mitchell, who battled double teams all night, only had three shots from the field, all misses, by halftime. Trent Pierce and Jacob Crews had combined for a 1-of-7 mark from 3-point range. T.O. Barrett went 0-of-6 from the field. The Hurricanes were battering the Tigers on the boards and cruised to a 10-point lead, capitalizing on second-chance looks and buckets despite Missouri's stellar initial interior defense.If a comeback was coming, it was going to need to come from somewhere else.And, for a while, it did. Robinson, who has been mired in an inexplicable slump for most of the year, gave Missouri a fighting chance with some individual excellence.The Tigers cut a once-10-point deficit to just one point courtesy of a 9-0 run in the final three minutes of the first half, as Robinson got Dennis Gates to throw a knee-jerk fist pump after a coast-to-coast layup and to bear hug an official to call a timeout after the point guard connected on a heavily contested triple.It looked possible. It always does.Again, though, Missouri is going home after one song at the Big Dance. The crowd that packed the St. Louis stands had mostly filtered out by the final minute of gametime.The Tigers have won just one game in the NCAA Tournament since 2010.Mizzou finished the 2025-26 season 20-13 after four straight losses.Missouri basketball live score vs Miami in NCAA TournamentThis section will be updated when the game begins. U4 timeout: Miami 63, Missouri 57The Tigers need something special. Miami had a massive run, 11-0, to separate again after MU took the lead.U8 timeout: Missouri leadsMark Mitchell drills a 3 for the lead. Points to his forearm, where there sure is ice in those veins.Jayden Stone and Ant Robinson are fighting like hell here. Just phenomenal performances from the guards in a massive moment.What a remarkable game. U12 timeout: Miami 46, Missouri 43Mizzou keeps letting possessions to go ahead slip by. Dennis Gates just turned to his bench and said "we're right there."Are they? There have been some truly terrible shots in the past few minutes. Missouri is getting its chances. The crowd is willing it on. Let's see. U16 timeout: Miami 37, Missouri 32Mizzou briefly tied the game with a pair of Shawn Phillips dunks — a good plan if Miami is going to double Mitchell with big men all night. But the Hurricanes are back up by five courtesy of a Tre Donaldson 3-pointer. Half: Maimi 27, Missouri 26.Anthony Robinson came alive in the last few minutes to cut a 10-point deficit to just one. Missouri is alive, and the crowd is back onside.Honestly, the way this game was going, pretty sure Mizzou would have liked another 5 minutes in this half. U4 timeout: Miami 26, Missouri 17The Hurricanes are pulling away as Mizzou has missed each of its past eight shots. Miami can take a double-digit lead with a trip to the free throw line coming after the break. U8 timeout: Miami 21, Missouri 17Fun, fun game here. Pace is fast. Neither team is giving an inch on the inside. Making those 3s is going to be so important tonight, and Miami is doing that better so far.Jayden Stone leads with seven points. Mark Mitchell only has one shot attempt. Miami is doing a fantastic job guarding him. U12 timeout: Miami 12, Mizzou 10Jayden Stone was really trying to rile up the crowd, it looked like, after finally getting a 3-ball to fall. Missouri is getting looks on offense from the perimeter. They hadn't really been falling until then. Eight of Mizzou's 12 shots have been from 3, which is because Miami is sending double after double to Mark Mitchell.Tigers within two because of what has still been a good defensive start. U16 timeout: Miami 5, Missouri 2A wonderful start from the Missouri defense, which has impacted all but two of Miami's opening seven shots from the field, has been undone by a rather dreadful opening five on offense. The Tigers have turned it over three times and have started 1-of-6 from the field with three misses from 3-point range.Fast game so far, but Missouri needs to be more careful in possession in these next few minutes or the Canes could start running. The action is almost underway in St. LouisWe're about 10 minutes out now from the beginning of the final game of the first round: Missouri versus Miami in St. Louis.Sounds a lot like a home game in here. The crowd just roared as Mizzou came out of the tunnel. A pretty massive MIZ-ZOU is ringing around the arena now.The winner tonight will play 2-seed Purdue on Sunday. Let's have some fun. The Tigers are in the arenaMiami entered the Enterprise Center first, and was met with a pretty resounding chorus of boos from what was still a pretty heavy Purdue-leaning crowd. Seats are also beginning to fill up with a good portion of Missouri fans.The Tigers ran out of the tunnel shortly afterward. Missouri vs Miami looks like it will start on timePurdue vs Queens is flying by. At 8:07 p.m., the game is out of the Under-12 media timeout. The Boilermakers also are up by 22 points and neither team has more than three fouls in this half so far.That's a good sign — knock on wood — for Mizzou vs. Miami to begin at its designated 9:10 p.m. tipoff slot on truTV. Starting lineups set for Missouri vs MiamiWe're still more than one hour away from tipoff between Missouri and Miami, but the starting lineups are out.No changes for Mizzou tonight: TO Barrett, Jayden Stone, Trent Pierce, Mark Mitchell, Shawn Phillips Jr.Miami: Tre Donaldson, Dante Allen, Shelton Henderson, Malik Reneau, Ernest Udeh Jr.What TV channel is Missouri vs Miami in March Madness first roundTV Channel: truTVStream: SlingMissouri basketball’s game against Miami in the NCAA Tournament Round of 64 will air on truTV. The game will be available to stream on Sling.The broadcast crew on truTV will be Spero Dedes as the play-by-play announcer, Jim Spanarkel as the analyst and Jon Rothstein as the sideline reporter.Stream Missouri basketball with SlingWhat time does Missouri play Miami in 2026 NCAA tournament?Date: Friday, March 20Time: 9:10 p.m. CDTLocation: Enterprise Center in St. LouisMizzou’s game against Miami in the first round of the NCAA Tournament will take place at 9:10 p.m. CDT on Friday, March 20 in St. Louis. It will be the last game of the first round to tip off.How to listen to Friday’s gameSatellite radio: Tiger Radio Network / XM: 208 or 201 / SXM App: 963Tiger Radio Network will air the game live with Mike Kelly as the play-by-play announcer and Chris Gervino as the analyst. Fans can also tune in via the SiriusXM app, channel 963, or via XM channels 208 or 201 for the Westwood One broadcast, which features Nate Gatter as the play-by-play announcer and Jordan Cornette as the analyst.Missouri injury and availability updatesMizzou is likely to be without power forward Jevon Porter, who has not played since Dec. 14. The Tigers also will be missing Annor Boateng, who was ruled out for the season.Miami wing and former Missouri basketball freshman Marcus Allen, who was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin lymphoma in December, was ruled out for the season while he undergoes chemotherapy.The Hurricanes also will be without freshman Trevyon Maddox, who has not played this season.Score prediction: Miami 76, Missouri 72Can Missouri win this matchup? We watched the Tigers take down the reigning national champions, win at Rupp Arena, beat one of the most physical teams we’ve seen all season in Tennessee, take down BuckyBall on the road, and knock off SEC Tournament runner-up Vanderbilt.Yes, Missouri can win this matchup.But we are spooked by the last three games that Mizzou put together. The trio of losses were often tough viewing, and they threatened to derail a wonderful month of February.That hasn’t happened. Missouri is getting an opportunity to rebound, and to do so in its home state in front of a crowd that likely will have a gold-and-black lean.If Mizzou gets the job done, we will not be surprised, but
